Class ByteWriter

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.io.ByteWriter
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, Flushable, AutoCloseable
public final class ByteWriter extends Object implements Closeable, Flushable
Writes a stream of bytes: numbers in either byte order, runs of bytes and text.

A writer holds a buffer, which it writes to its stream when it is full, on flush() and on close(). Every write method returns the writer, so calls chain.

Methods that write a number write it in big-endian order, as DataOutputStream does; those whose name ends in Le write it in little-endian order. Methods that take an int for a smaller type write its low bits. 

try (var out = ByteSink.of(file).openWriter()) {
    out.write(MAGIC).writeShort(VERSION).writeIntLe(entries.size());
    for (var entry : entries) {
        out.writeLongLe(entry.offset()).writeString(entry.name()).writeByte(0);
    }
}

A writer owns its stream: close() closes it, and any write after that throws IOException. A writer is not safe for use by several threads at once.

Since:
0.1.3
